paper.title: From Pixels to UI Actions: Learning to Follow Instructions via Graphical User Interfaces
paper.central_claim: An agent using only pixel screenshots and a generic mouse/keyboard action space (Pix2Act: Pix2Struct initialisation, BC on human demonstrations, iterative MCTS policy improvement) outperforms human crowdworkers on MiniWob++ and is comparable to DOM-based SOTA; it establishes the first pixel-only WebShop baseline; screenshot-parsing pretraining is the key ingredient (authors' claim).

G.reason: Specific bottleneck: GUI agents depend on DOM/HTML and task-specific actions that are often unavailable; pixel-only generic-action agents were far weaker (CC-Net reported drop without DOM, A03; Pix2Act's own non-pretrained BC 17.1, A05). Lineage (WoB -> DOM-specialised agents -> CC-Net -> Pix2Struct; LLM HTML agents ReAct/RCI/WebGUM) is laid out in §6. Not 4: the closest pixel-only comparator is an extrapolated 75% drop rather than a measured run (A04), and the CC-Net/Pix2Struct originals are not in the fixed reference set, so the residual gap is bounded only by the paper's account. Both seats agree.

M.reason: Operation reconstructable and aimed at the bottleneck: screenshot-parsing pretraining supplies visual UI priors, a generic discretised mouse/keyboard token space removes DOM dependence, MCTS with reward/reset generates better trajectories that are distilled back by SFT. Distinguishable predictions exist (no-pretraining collapse, greedy improves after distillation). Not 4: whether gains come from parsing pretraining vs. scale/data, and search vs. any reward-filtered self-training, is not isolated. Both seats agree.

X.reason: Observation construction (rendered instruction, cursor, button state), action binning, beam/anti-cycle greedy policy, MCTS (K=16, top-8, lambda mixing), value net source, reward filter and 2 SFT rounds are all specified; training-time privileges (reset, reward) are explicit; excluded task families listed with reasons. Not 4: evaluation step cap not stated (A11, A38), LR descriptions inconsistent (A36), held-out list 9 vs 8 names (I02), only anti-cycle recovery and no history (A30, A31). Both seats agree.

E.measurement.reason: Programmatic MiniWoB++ reward over 59 tasks x 100 seeds with timeouts scored 0 and a full per-task table; WebShop standard 500-instruction test split with its automatic reward. Not 4: human and CC-Net numbers come from a different real-time X11 harness (A20, A21), the pixel-only prior-work point is extrapolated (A04), and comparator WebShop values are figure-only. Both seats agree.

E.causality.reason: The paper's causal claims each have a within-paper control on the same harness: pretraining vs random init under BC on in-task MiniWoB++ (17.1 -> 66.5), held-out tasks (7.6 -> 28.3) and WebShop (1.1 -> 46.7) (A05, A16, A17); same-model greedy vs search and per-iteration greedy gains (A06, A07); leaf-evaluation ablation (A28); intermediate-finetuning ablation (A23). Gains are large relative to the evaluation-seed spread. Residual alternatives: search vs. plain reward-filtered self-training at equal episodes (A24, A08), measured no-DOM baseline (A04), same-backbone DOM arm. These bound the tree-search attribution, not the existence of the improvement; hence 3 rather than 2 (sol) or 4.

E.holdout.reason: Main evaluation uses fresh random seeds of the same 59 tasks the tree-search data were generated on (A09); task-level holdout exists only for BC and is author-picked (A14, A15, I02); WebShop uses the standard test split (A35). No unseen site/app for the full search-trained policy. Both seats agree.

E.statistics.reason: Denominators are explicit and complete (59 tasks x 100 seeds, timeouts = 0, selection of 59/104 declared as feasibility-based with per-family exclusion lists, A10, A11, A13), a per-task table exposes every weak task, and three evaluation-seed resamplings of the headline model give SD 0.15 (A12), which makes the 1.9-pt margin over the human mean robust to evaluation sampling. Not 4: no training-run replicates, no spread for other configurations or WebShop, human reference from another harness. 3 (sol) rather than 2 (son55): the missing replicates concern training variance, while uncertainty and denominators for the reported comparisons are better covered than the 2-anchor 'key statistical gaps' description.

E.cost.reason: Model size (282M), training steps (26K+26K), 826K search episodes, 64 TPUv3 cores and search budget (K=16, top-8) reported (A08, A26, A27); no wall-clock, inference latency, or matched-budget comparison with baselines. Both seats agree.
